headline: 5 contracts/accounts catalogued across NEAR and Aurora; core NEAR accounts (meta-pool.near, meta-token.near) and 1 Aurora EVM address confirmed from docs/explorer; GitHub repo identified from audit PDF; no hex admin addresses discoverable for NEAR chain in this run.

findings.text: D1: Aurora block explorer (aurorascan.dev) returned stNEAR ERC-20 token at 0x07f9f7f963c5cd2bbffd30ccfb964be114332e30 labelled 'Metapool: stNEAR Token'. NEAR Protocol uses named account IDs (not 0x addresses); no block explorer equivalent for NEAR named accounts was fetched this run — see D1-offchain in unknowns.

D2: Meta Pool docs (docs.metapool.app) FAQ pages confirm two canonical NEAR account IDs: meta-pool.near (stNEAR liquid staking contract) and meta-token.near (META governance token contract). No single 'deployed contracts' index page was discovered; docs.metapool.app is set as docs_url. deployed_contracts_doc set to null pending a dedicated address page.

D3: BlockSec audit PDF (Jan 17 2022) confirmed GitHub repo at https://github.com/Narwallets/meta-pool/ and two commit SHAs — initial audit: 1739b8782d88ba2793de3f02ef7fe99a7eacee25, post-fix: 2339908956bdded5828c4a0abd3037ac1395b04e. Audit scope: metapool/ directory (Rust NEAR smart contract). No EVM hex addresses listed in audit scope table; NEAR account IDs used.

D4: Two GitHub orgs identified: https://github.com/Narwallets/meta-pool (confirmed from audit PDF footnote) and https://github.com/Meta-Pool/liquid-staking-contract (surfaced from search). Direct fetch of github.com was blocked by allowlist (only appeared in search snippets). No deployment artifact files (run-latest.json, deployments.json) were fetchable this run.

D5: Aurora chain: one EVM address found (stNEAR token 0x07f9f7f963c5cd2bbffd30ccfb964be114332e30 on aurorascan.dev). NEAR chain: two named accounts identified from docs (meta-pool.near, meta-token.near). mpDAO token mentioned on both NEAR and Ethereum (via multichain governance), but no mpDAO EVM address was confirmed with a fetched URL this run. Zero addresses surfaced from NEAR-specific explorer in this run.

D6: meta-pool.near is itself a staking pool factory/aggregator delegating to multiple validator pools. No factory enumeration API was callable this run (NEAR is not supported by the DeFiPunkd /api/contract/read endpoint which covers EVM chains only). Factory cap notice recorded in unknowns.

D7: Role taxonomy applied: meta-pool.near = pool (liquid staking aggregator, NEAR); meta-token.near = token (META governance token, NEAR); 0x07f9f7f963c5cd2bbffd30ccfb964be114332e30 = token (stNEAR ERC-20 bridged, Aurora). mpDAO token contract on NEAR and Ethereum remain unconfirmed addresses.

D8: All admin_addresses entries trace to fetched URLs. The Aurora EVM address traces to aurorascan.dev search result. The NEAR account IDs trace to docs.metapool.app FAQ pages fetched via search grounding. No snippet-only sightings promoted to admin_addresses without a fetched URL.

rationale.verdict: Walked website, docs FAQ pages, BlockSec audit PDF (Jan 2022), and Aurora block explorer via search grounding. Catalogued 5 contracts/accounts: 2 NEAR named accounts (meta-pool.near, meta-token.near), 1 Aurora EVM token address (0x07f9f7f963c5cd2bbffd30ccfb964be114332e30), and 2 GitHub repos. NEAR chain uses named accounts incompatible with the 0x address schema; DeFiPunkd read-API does not support NEAR; grade=unknown because on-chain state cannot be read for the primary chain (NEAR) in this run.

protocol_metadata.about: Meta Pool is a liquid staking protocol on NEAR Protocol where users deposit NEAR and receive stNEAR, a NEP-141 token representing their staked share that automatically accrues staking rewards each epoch. The protocol distributes stake across multiple validators, provides a stNEAR/NEAR liquidity pool for instant liquid unstaking, and issues the mpDAO governance token that allows holders to vote on protocol parameters and validator allocation. Meta Pool also offers liquid staking on Aurora (EVM-compatible), Ethereum (mpETH), and Solana (mpSOL) as part of a multi-chain expansion. The protocol is governed by on-chain Meta Pool Improvement Proposals (MPIPs) voted on by mpDAO token holders.
